Last month, after the TV tracking app TV Time ceased operations, one of its co-founders, Antonio Pinto, announced the launch of a brand-new film and TV tracking app called Bingers, which places greater emphasis on social features. Here are the details.

Bingers is now available for download

When Whip Media announced it would be shutting down the TV tracking app TV Time, one of the co-founders promptly launched Bingers, positioning it as a "fast, beautiful watchlist with a fun community."

As reported by TechCrunch, Bingers is now available for download on iOS and Android, offering a spiritual successor for users who have yet to find a replacement. At its peak, TV Time was one of the most widely used TV tracking apps in the world.

Former TV Time users who backed up their data using the platform's export tool before the app shut down can import their databases into Bingers, seamlessly continuing their previous records. As for users who did not export their data at the time, or newcomers who have never used a TV tracking app before, they can start fresh from scratch.

Bingers has significantly enhanced its community interaction features, including personal profiles, comments, episode ratings, GIF animations, polls, and character popularity votes. Pinto told TechCrunch that these features are precisely what made TV Time so popular over the years:

If users simply want a platform to log the shows and movies they have watched, Bingers also offers dedicated watchlist and viewing history features. Just like TV Time, the platform includes a calendar for new episodes and premiere dates, showing how many days remain until broadcast.

Bingers is available for free on the App Store and currently does not include any in-app purchases.
